problem:
Given the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]$, 
find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{-1}AP.$

feedback.problem: Find matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=B,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix and $B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.** We need to find the eigenvalues of the matrix $B$ using its characteristic equation $det(B-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 \\ -1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(-2-\lambda )-2\cdot (-1) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda +1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $B$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=0$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ 

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $B.$

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B-0I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=-1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ={R}_{2}+(\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=-1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$
